content.title: About
content.content: Pork loin, boneless, raw is a lean cut taken from the back of the pig. It is known for its mild flavor, tender texture, and low fat content compared with other pork cuts. In its raw state the meat is light pink with a slightly moist sheen.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The loin is the leanest pork cut and is often chosen for low‑fat diets.
Because of its tenderness it is sometimes called pork “tenderloin”.
Raw pork loin can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and frozen for up to 6 months.
When cooked properly the loin stays juicy and does not dry out.
Different cuisines feature the loin: in the US as pork tenderloin roast, in Japan as part of tonkatsu.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The loin contains about 3–4 g of fat per 100 g, making it a good protein source for low‑fat eating plans.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Provides roughly 20–22 g of complete protein per 100 g, essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains zinc, selenium and iron, important for immune health and blood formation.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: Approximately 120 kcal per 100 g, useful for energy balance control.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Raw pork may harbor pathogens such as Salmonella or Trichinella; it must be cooked to an internal temperature of 63 °C.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals can experience allergic reactions to pork.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: When cured, brined, or seasoned, sodium levels can become high, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Additives in processed products
items.content: Pre‑marinated or pre‑seasoned loin pieces may contain preservatives and flavor enhancers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The loin can be roasted, grilled, pan‑seared, or braised. It is often marinated in olive oil, herbs, garlic, and spices before cooking. Slice thinly for salads, sandwiches, or serve as a steak‑like main dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw pork loin in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a vacuum‑sealed bag for up to 6 months. Thaw frozen loin in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.
